title: Panda's Grandfather
paragraphs: And then the next day… I think I heard a loud thud. When I woke up and went outside for some fresh air, sure enough, Old Man Panda was holding a training session with Panda and Éclair.

…And Elephant is there too. He’s sitting on his butt, and there’s a crater in the ground. Father and Sakura-chan seem to be watching the spectacle. Perhaps they’re having a mock battle, because Old Man Panda is standing in a fighting stance with his huge pipe drawn. Panda, Éclair, and even the elephant all look a bit worn out.
“Their movements are quite fast, but that makes them a bit monotonous. I thought I was in a tight spot there, too.”
The old panda says this cheerfully while twirling his pipe around.
“I was holding back because I didn’t want them to neglect their technique while focusing on leveling up and improving their stats… but to be cornered like this and not even be left out of breath…”
“Your skills are still monstrous as ever.”
“I fought him thinking it’d be like facing Larsa, but I never expected to get thrown like that…”
Zou said as he got back to his feet. To throw a giant like that—he’s quite the fighter.
“Wow!”
Sakura-chan looks a little sleepy since it’s early in the morning, but she’s sharing her thoughts on the battle.
“Elmero, he was flying!”
Kou’s eyes sparkled as he talked about how Zou had been flying. Sakura-chan and Kou are loving it. Even I could throw him across the room!
“That’s amazing.”
“It’s not that big of a deal. Truth be told, I’m just copying what I’ve seen.”
The Old Panda replied to Father, who was praising him.
“Look, Rasa. Your job is to guard the Shield Hero, isn’t it? Do you really think you can protect him with a performance like that?”
“Shut up. Even without me protecting him, this guy’s rock-solid!”
Saying that, Panda stands up, brushes the sand off, and takes a fighting stance against the Old Panda. Looks like they’re still going to fight, huh?
“I’m going to go faster than before!”
Panda pulls out a bamboo stalk and, using the recoil, charges forward with a brute-force attack powered by his level.
“That’s why I keep telling you your moves are too predictable!”

Whoosh… Something like Ki surged from the Old Man Panda’s body. He smoothly dodged the Panda’s charge, then swept his pipe through the air, sending the Panda flying. Whoa… The Panda soared high into the air.
“Waaaaaaaaaaah!?”
With a thud, the panda plummeted straight down.
“As expected of Lord Lasa’s grandfather… Perhaps I should seek his guidance for the battles ahead? His technique is that polished.”
“I’d rather you cut me some slack…”
“Or rather, such skill reminds me of Lord Kitamura…”
Hmm… I suppose I should show Father just how strong I am right here. Since Father from the first world warned me, I’ve been honing not just my level, but my technique as well.
“It’s my turn, then.”
“Motoyasu, even though he’s strong, he’s an old man, so please go easy on him—or rather, don’t kill him, okay?”
“Of course.”
“Oh? Is the Spear Hero going to face me?”
The old panda, with his pipe resting on his shoulder, beckons me over. Since he seems to be using a long weapon, I suppose we can fight on somewhat similar terms?
“Well then, here I go. Of course… this will be a battle of skill.”
It would be tacky to just brute-force my way through with my level just to gauge his skill. I’ll hold back a bit, too.
“Let’s see what the Spear Hero is made of.”
Sure enough, the old panda’s catchphrase has crept into his speech.
“Here we gooooo!”
The old panda swings his pipe at me. I dodge it, but I can sense that he’s using an upward slashing motion while simultaneously weaving his Ki into the strike to entangle me.
“Whoa, there.”
It also feels like he’s channeling Ki toward me to make it harder for me to brace myself. So I mix Ki into my spear to counter while parrying his attack, and in turn, I channel my own Ki back at him.
“Oh?”

I spin my spear to parry his attack, and the Old Panda immediately transitions into a thrust, trying to pull me in as if to scratch me. But I deflect that too, thrust my spear into the ground to create distance, and in turn, jab him in the torso with the stone tip. Of course, I weave Ki into it so he’ll be sent flying even farther.
“Whoa… this is amazing. My blood is boiling.”

The Old Man in the Panda Costume taps the ground with his pipe to divert my momentum as I’m sent flying, then lands and charges right at me. This time, it looks like a fluid combination of a body-check and a kick.
“W-w-wait a minute!”

I read his move and block it, but using my spear as a pivot, the Old Man Panda attempts a sweep followed by a spin throw. What an acrobatic panda. In terms of skill alone, isn’t he on par with not just Takt, but even Big Sister’s older sister? I fluidly parry that throw, land, and then swing the spinning old panda around before tossing him myself.
“Whoa! Not done yet!”

With an incredibly joyful grin, the old panda comes charging after me. His tenacity is incredible. It feels like he’s really enjoying the fight. And each of his attacks is infused with Ki. An inexperienced fighter wouldn’t stand a chance against this.
“Ooooh… Hah, hah…”

After that, I took a few more hits while occasionally counterattacking, but I couldn’t land a decisive blow. Just as the old panda stepped back to create some distance, he ran out of breath and began resting, using his pipe as a cane. My skill level is such that if I’d been a bit more aggressive, subduing him would’ve been easy. His technique is only slightly weaker than that of Big Sister from the first world.
“I’ve certainly witnessed the Spear Hero’s skill… Haa… Haa…”
The match is over.
“To go this far against an old man—the Spear Hero really is a monster, isn’t he?”
“I’ll admit that’s true in more ways than one.”
“How does he manage to pull off attacks and defenses like that?”
“His movements were just like something out of a kung fu movie. It looked like he was doing wire stunts or something.”
Fathers-in-law, who had been watching the sparring session between the Panda Elder and me, each shared their impressions. Their reactions were quite positive.
“His movements are remarkably fluid. Did you learn that somewhere?”

“Haa… haa… No, as I said earlier, I just picked it up by watching and imitating. A long time ago, on the battlefield against Melromarc, I fought a guy who was strong like a monster countless times. As I kept doing that, I naturally picked up similar movements and a similar flow of power—that’s how I developed my own style…”

So he fought strong opponents over and over, learned their movements, and refined them into his own fighting style. To call that “self-taught” is pretty amazing. I suppose I’m self-taught in a sense, too. It’s hard for me to tell whether I’m using my Ki consciously or unconsciously, though.
“I wonder how long ago it was… I really missed him after he stopped showing up on the battlefield…”
The old panda muttered wistfully. I suppose he must have been killed in action.

“To think I’d get to fight in one of those heart-pounding, blood-pumping battles again… I suppose it’s my age… no, maybe I just haven’t trained hard enough. It wouldn’t be so bad to get back into it in earnest… Lasa, I know you’re running away because you don’t want to learn from me, but is it really okay to just let things stay this way?”
“Give me a break. Just how much are you expecting from me? Besides, if anything happens, won’t the Spear Hero just sweep everything away anyway?”
“When I think back on the last war, I can’t exactly deny that…”
“That’s no excuse for slacking off. I was even thinking of asking you to come to the castle as a combat advisor so I could learn from you.”
“I’d rather not get thrown around every day, but I do think we should spread this style for the sake of Siltvelt’s future.”
Éclair and Zou are trying to get lessons from the Old Panda. The Panda’s face is turning into a “Ugh” expression.
“Isn’t it better to have the Spear Hero, since he’s the more skilled one?”
“If it’s about fighting, I can teach you, too.”
This is a great opportunity to show Father just how capable I am.
“Well, Motoyasu-kun is busy with his Idol activities, so he probably doesn’t have the time, does he?”
Come to think of it, that’s true. My mission is to support the idol activities of the Filolial-sama. I really need to take it easy on my days off.
“Well, I’ve recorded the portal, so we can go back and forth anytime now. Lars-chan can also go back to her parents’ house with peace of mind.”
“That’s a bit of a downer, though…”
“Either way, Spear Hero, I’d love for you to spar with me again if the chance arises.”
“Yeah. I’ll ask you to do it for everyone’s sake, too.”
“Since Father asked me, I can’t very well refuse.”

It seems Father will praise me if I fight, so I’ll go ahead and spar with him. Above all, Sakura-chan and Kou are watching me with such delighted eyes! It’ll be nice to show everyone just how cool I am. So, that’s how we ended up visiting Panda’s parents’ house and coming back.
“—That’s pretty much how it went.”

Father was explaining the whole situation to Rival, who’d come over for dinner at Siltvelt Castle, as if sharing a travel story. Oh, and of course, this was right in front of Panda. It was the kind of explanation that stayed within the limits Panda would allow. Maybe Panda figures it’s okay since it’s just a friend—he’s just eating his meal in silence.
“W-what…?”
And now, Rival who’d been listening to Father is pressing a hand to his forehead. What’s the matter? Did he eat something poisoned and is about to die? Serves him right.
“Hey, Spear Hero. Don’t you have anything to say?”
“About what, exactly?”
“You’re totally playing dumb there.”

For some reason, Rival is giving me a look like he’s mocking me! What’s that about! Is he planning to find another excuse to put me down again! This guy is definitely trying to bring me down after I gained some status from training with Panda’s grandfather.
“It was kind of the same with Raph, too. Could it be that you’re doing this on purpose?”
“I don’t understand what you mean.”
Why is Big Sister coming up in this conversation? She shouldn’t have anything to do with this at all.
“Panda, haven’t you heard that Hakuko’s wife is human?”
“Hmm… I’ve heard it secondhand, I guess. They say Hakuko’s half-human.”
“That’s definitely true.”
“So what’s the point?”
Rival is being way too cryptic—it’s infuriating.
“Gaelion-chan, do you know something?”
“I do. In fact, I’ve met her not only in Ofumi’s wild world but in other loops as well.”
“Was there someone like that? The people I know are pretty limited.”
Who are you talking about? I remember what the Hakuko clan is like, but the only ones I know are the tiger girl who bravely defended Filolial-sama—starting with Father—and her pathetic older brother.
“The Spear Hero—that’s the one you’re picturing in your mind. The tiger siblings.”
“No, no, the world is just too big for that. It’s definitely not them!”

“Why can’t you make the connection?!　You really are an idiot! A brother and sister with a seriously ill younger sister who’ve gone off somewhere—the Hakuko Clan is such a distinctive group; it’s definitely those two!”
“Stop calling me an idiot! The one calling me an idiot is the real idiot! You’re the fool!”
“Motoyasu-kun…”
Father is looking at Rival and me with a gaze as if he’s looking at some pitiful creatures. See, Rival? You’re the idiot here!
“Since the timing’s right, we should just take them under our protection.”
“No, please wait a moment.”
At this point, the representative of the Shusaku clan—who had been silent until now—raises his hand.
“Given that they are of mixed blood, I think it would be best to avoid having the Shield Hero directly take the Hakuko Clan under his protection, if at all possible.”
“Is that… um, perhaps because of the domestic situation?”
When Father asked, the representative of the Shusaku Clan nodded.

“Yes. It’s largely because they’ve achieved military feats recognized by the nation that the Shield Hero’s companions are accepted in their current form. If someone affiliated with the four representative races of Siltvelt were to join them now, it would inevitably involve matters of power…”
It seems it’ll be difficult for Father to take care of the tiger siblings. Between tradition and the political climate, Siltvelt is quite a hassle in this regard.

“As for the events in the alternate timeline the Spear Heroes are discussing—not only are they heavily tied to what happened in Melromarc, but I suspect another reason is that the Shield Hero’s approval ratings hadn’t risen yet… Right now, within Siltvelt, the Heroes’ standing is rising rapidly—not just because of their actions in the war, but also because of their efforts to calm the unrest… so…”
“Yeah, I get what you’re saying, so don’t worry.”

He showed understanding toward the Shusaku race, whom Father was so concerned about. Well, there are surely various ways to go about it. In fact, in the loop I went through before, I left him with Trash.
“It’s not like I’m expecting you to protect me or anything, you know?”
“That’s not the only reason, you know.”
It seems Rival is pushing even harder here. You’re pretty persistent, aren’t you?
“Gaelion-chan, is there some other reason?”
“Of course there is. Or rather, I was planning to bring this up soon anyway, so this is perfect timing.”
Rival nods here and then looks at me.
“To begin with, with the Spear Hero… and the Wise King of Wisdom still out there, why aren’t you doing anything?”
It’s hard to tell who’s in the know about these matters in Siltvelt. Only a few of the Trash have gone rusty, escaped, and are operating in the shadows.
